title: Levered ETFs Are New Way To Measure Sentiment: Sohn
summary:
Todd Sohn, chief ETF strategist at Baird Strategas, joins Scarlet Fu and James Seyffart on "ETF IQ." They discuss leveraged ETFs, the recent rush of thematic filings, and the risk the tied to concentrated portfolios.
 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trade Data Hasn't Caught Up With Trump Policy Changes, Says Peter Harrell
summary: Peter Harrell, former White House senior director for international economics in the Biden Administration and visiting scholar at Georgetown, said President Trump has not brought tariff rates back to their original rate because war with Iran has driven energy prices higher. Harrell also said that while US trade and investment policy has changed, the data coming into the administration and out to the public has not yet caught up and it remains an question what the impact of these changes will be. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Copper Market Squeeze Intensifies as More Metal Is Shipped to US
summary: A surge in copper shipments to the US in anticipation of a potential decision to impose import tariffs is creating a severe market squeeze, pushing global prices close to a record high as buyers scramble to secure supplies.

title: Bolivia Hikes Diesel Prices for Big Buyers to Tame Supply Shock
summary: Bolivia’s government raised diesel prices 84% for larger consumers of the key industrial fuel, following shortages that caused long lines at gas stations.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for June 17
summary: Oil climbed as indications that the Middle East conflict is long from settled dampened optimism that shipments through the Strait of Hormuz will expand to pre-war levels in the near future.

title: Stocks Fall as Brent Tops $90 on Middle East Risks: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks and bonds fell on concern that elevated oil prices will fuel inflation as hopes for a deal to end the almost six-month war in the Middle East faded.

title: Blackstone, Blue Owl Private Credit Funds Boost Bond Sales
summary: Two private credit funds sold more investment-grade bonds Monday than they initially targeted, following a lull of deals from so-called business development companies to start the third quarter.

title: US High-Grade Bond Sales Set August Record in Year Full of Them
summary: US investment-grade bond sales have set a third straight monthly record, continuing the market’s fastest pace of issuance as spending on the artificial-intelligence buildout fuels corporate borrowing.

title: Iran Feels It Has 'New Leverage' In MidEast Amid War with US
summary: Michael Allen, managing director of Beacon Global Strategies and a former national security aide to President George W. Bush, said Iranians feel they have "a lot of new leverage" they didn't have before the US and Israel launched strikes as Iran's government looks to rebuild its influence in the region. Allen also discussed President Trump's decision to pull back on military exercises with South Korea, saying he doesn't know what South Korea has done to deserve a chilling in US-South Korea relations.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Bond Selloff Drives 30-Year Yields to Highest Since 2007
summary: The yield on 30-year US Treasuries hit the highest in almost two decades, reflecting investor angst over surging government spending, a flood of long-dated bond sales, and inflation that’s been stuck over the Federal Reserve’s target for the past five years.

title: Microsoft-Tied ‘Project Odyssey’ Bond Lures Buyers at Junk Yield
summary: A corporate-bond sale dubbed “Project Odyssey” may be increased to $3.9 billion as junk-like yields on the Microsoft Corp.-linked data-center financing drew more than twice that amount in demand.

title: Traders Alert for Deeper Bond Rout Fueling Niche Arbitrage Trade
summary: An extended selloff in the $31 trillion US government bond market is opening the door for a potentially lucrative trade that profits from pricing shifts between derivatives and their underlying cash bonds.

title: The Two Megatrends Changing the US Treasury Market
summary: Heading for higher yields.

title: Hydro-Quebec Inks $36 Billion Energy Deal With Newfoundland
summary: The Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador managed to boost the value of a new 50-year electricity supply agreement with Hydro-Quebec, likely ending a long-running dispute.

title: US Stocks Dip as Rising Oil Prices, Yields Offset Chip Gains
summary: US stocks faltered on Monday as long-term Treasury yields extended their recent climb and oil ticked higher. Chipmakers notched gains as details of Anthropic’s surging sales growth stoked bullish sentiment around AI.

title: Guggenheim Ties Sink Bonds of $135 Billion Life Insurer Sammons
summary: Bonds of Sammons Financial Group fell to the lowest since they were issued in June after a report probed the life insurer’s connections to Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners.

title: Dollar Extends Slide as Traders Scale Back Fed Tightening Bets
summary: The dollar fell to its weakest level in three months as investors scaled back expectations for further Federal Reserve interest-rate increases following a run of softer US economic data.

title: Emerging Currencies Rise as Traders Cut Bets on Fed Rate Hikes
summary: Emerging-market currencies gained as easing bets on a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next month undercut the dollar and supported risk appetite.

title: Walter Rushes Makeover as DOJ Probes His Empire
summary: The CEO of Guggenheim Partners and owner of the LA Dodgers flipped the Lakers within a year and has explored other steps to pay down loans from his insurers. Bloomberg's Sridhar Natarajan joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Vitol Makes Push Into Data-Center Infrastructure With US Deal
summary: Vitol said its renewables arm had acquired a data center campus in South Carolina from Meridan Gridworks, one of the first instances of a major commodity trader delving into artificial intelligence infrastructure.
